intent: Ordered wizard steps as numbered circles with a connecting line and a status word under each label: Done, Current, Upcoming, Error, or Optional. Completed steps can be buttons. Horizontal switches to a compact Step n of m with a Progress bar in a narrow container. Vertical for side columns. One piece.
useWhen: A required sequence the user walks through in order
Numbered steps with complete, current, and upcoming
doNotUseWhen: A determinate percent 0 to 100 — use Progress
A vertical now/next/later roadmap — use Timeline
Peer views the user can switch freely — use Tabs
Paging a list or table — use Pagination
A first-run checklist people can skip or do in any order — use SetupGuide

steps.note: { id, label, description?, status?: complete|current|upcoming|error, optional? }[]. Status is derived from current when omitted. optional: an upcoming optional step gets a dashed marker and the word Optional.

current.note: 0-based index of the current step. Pass steps.length to mark every step complete.

orientation.note: horizontal is the default. In a container narrower than 30rem it shows Step n of m, the current label, and a kit Progress bar labelled with the next step. vertical stacks marker, then copy, for a side column or drawer.

onStepClick.note: (index, step) => void. When set, completed steps become buttons named by their label. Upcoming steps stay inert and out of the tab order.

requirements: nav with aria-label Progress or ariaLabel
Marker is aria-hidden; the visible status word matches the announcement: Done, Current, Upcoming, Error, or Optional, with step n of m
With onStepClick, completed steps are buttons whose name includes the step label; upcoming steps are not in the tab order
The compact Progress bar always has a text label
Reduced motion turns off the marker and line colour transition

doNot: Do not invent StepItem, Stepper, ProgressStep, or Icon cousins
Do not use Progress for ordered wizard steps
Do not use Timeline for numbered checkout or onboarding steps
Do not use Tabs for a required sequence
Do not use ProgressSteps for a skippable first-run checklist — use SetupGuide
Do not make upcoming steps clickable
Do not put the Back and Continue footer inside ProgressSteps — compose it from kit Button, one primary
Do not copy Untitled UI CSS or hex
snippet: <ProgressSteps current={1} onStepClick={(index) => goTo(index)} steps={[{ id: 'plan', label: 'Plan' }, { id: 'billing', label: 'Billing' }, { id: 'addons', label: 'Add-ons', optional: true }, { id: 'review', label: 'Review' }]} />
